adds.title: LGBT rights in Colombia
adds.summary: National-framework page defining the legal regime a trans visitor to Guainía stands under: Colombia decriminalised homosexuality in 1981, Congress passed a law banning discrimination based on sexual orientation in 2011, and the Constitutional Court legalised same-sex marriage in a 6-3 ruling of 28 April 2016 (first wedding in Cali on 24 May 2016), having granted same-sex couples property, social-security and pension rights in three rulings between February 2007 and April 2008 and full adoption rights with dual-parent birth registration in November 2015. Since August 2023 passports issued within Colombia offer three gender options (male, female, X), and adults can change legal gender before a notary without surgery, with a free simultaneous name change on first request; gays, lesbians and bisexuals have served openly in the armed forces since a 1999 court ruling. The department adds no separate legal regime, so this page fixes the visitor's formal legal exposure against which the record's armed-group violence findings are weighed.
